findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the hero's black button 'Request a quote for swimwear accessories' sits almost on the tinted trust bar, with only a few pixels of white under it (at 390px it touches the bar), because the media-banner hero has no bottom padding of its own.
findings.reference: The competitor leaves a clear white gap of about 40px or more under its hero buttons ('Request Price', 'Book a Call') before the next section starts.
findings.fix: In template.css give .page-hero[data-variant="media-banner"] .page-hero__inner a bottom padding (e.g. calc(var(--section-space) / 2)) so the space under the button falls on the hero's own white ground, not inside the next block's tint.

findings.issue: featureGrid-1 is set out as a check list beside its heading directly under iconList-1, which already has that shape, so two sections of the same shape stand one under the other (m9, also a featureGrid set out as a list, and m10, an iconList, repeat this further down).
findings.reference: The site rule: when two sections of the same shape meet, the template sets only one of them out as a list beside its heading. The competitor never stacks two lists of the same layout.
findings.fix: In the template's same-shape check, count an iconList as already being a list beside its heading: a featureGrid next to an iconList keeps its card grid (featureGrid-1 after iconList-1, m9 before m10) rather than turning into a list.

findings.issue: On desktops the iconList item titles ('Standalone orders', 'Shipping options', 'Exposure and finish', 'Colour approval') are fitted to about 26px at weight 700 under a section heading of about 32px at weight 500, so the item level reads as heavy as the heading. The same lists set out by featureGrid (featureGrid-1, m9) use small bold titles, and the faq questions are also about 26px bold beside their 32px heading.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps its bold sub-heads ('Pricing Custom Swimwear Designs', 'Ready Designs', 'Custom Designs') just above body size, clearly under its section headings.
findings.fix: In the shared heading-fit step, cap the fitted size of an item h3 (icon-list item, faq question) at desktop widths too, e.g. at most ~0.65 of its section h2's fitted size, as was done on phones.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the related-links section is white directly after the white owner-testimonials section, so two plain sections in a row share one background while the rest of the page alternates white and tint.
findings.reference: The site rule: neighbouring plain sections alternate white and tinted backgrounds, set by the template.
findings.fix: In the template's surface alternation, count owner-testimonials (it follows the photo wall media-module-budget-1) so that related takes the --section-tint surface, or start the alternation again after the photo wall so that testimonials is tinted.

findings.issue: The related section carries about twice the top and bottom space of every other section (heading about 85px under the section edge on phones and about 100px on desktops, against about 50px elsewhere), which leaves an unexplained empty band before and after the link list.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps one even gap between its sections.
findings.fix: In template.css drop the extra padding on .block--related-pages (or .related-pages--grid) so that it uses the shared --section-space like its neighbours.

findings.issue: At 1440px the table's first column is only about 140px wide, so two-word labels break onto two lines ('Natural / shaping', 'Steel / underwires', 'Wire / protection', 'Grip / placement') while the specification column has room to spare. The table also stops about 130px short of the content's right edge.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps short labels on one line and lets its content blocks run the full text column.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css give .block--table .table-block th:first-child, td:first-child a min-width that fits its longest label (or white-space: nowrap above 900px), and let the table take the full content width.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: on phones the cost chart's label column takes about 40% of the panel, so values break into stacks of one or two words ('Custom- / moulded, / plus mould / fee', 'Standard / gold or / silver') and the header wraps as 'Lower / cost'.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps short figures on one or two lines on phones.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css narrow the chart's label column below 768px (e.g. th:first-child { width: 32%; }) and reduce the cells' inline padding, so each value keeps to two lines at most.

findings.issue: Two different check marks are used on this page: featureGrid sections set out as lists (featureGrid-1, m9) use a text '✓' marker that renders in a fallback serif font, unlike the drawn check icon of the iconList sections (iconList-1, iconList-2, m3, m10) next to them.
findings.reference: The competitor uses one marker style throughout a page.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css (line 266) replace the list-style-type '\2713' marker on .point-list__items with the same SVG check that .icon-list__icon draws (e.g. a ::before mask in var(--accent-text)), so both lists show one check.

findings.issue: The only text-and-photo row with a photo is drawn as a contained square photo next to its copy on the shared beige tint, so it does not look like the competitor's split module.
findings.reference: The competitor's split ('Sampling') sets its copy on a coloured blush panel, with the photo filling the other half to the page edge.
findings.fix: In template-variants.json give m7 the existing splitMedia variant 'panel' (already styled in src/styles/reference.css as the blush copy panel) so it follows the competitor's module.
